title: Older trumpet players whose chops last
summary: Dance and Edison note few of that generation still play well, with Roy Eldridge needing to warm up.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: How do you -- now, you know, if you take that generation, there are not many trumpet players left who can really play.
I mean, you are -- I was saying to somebody the other day, I mean, Roy has more or less got to warm up to it, doesn't he?

The third set of the night, he's doing right. But you've really -- you're almost the exception there. All those people like Shorty Baker and poor Taft, he's very well. Doc Cheatham is about the only other one.
Yeah, he's in his late 70's, too.
There's a thing about the chops that --
Do you do anything -- I mean, is there anything --
No, there's nothing you can do but just pray that they last a long time. That's all.
What happens? Do you ever get any soreness or --
